Measures
In this Psychology graduate student survey, there are three 3 question sets measuring different aspects of individual degree of social anxiety. SA, which refers to Social Interaction Anxiety Scale Question, (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.9). AA, which refers to Experiences in Close Relationships Anxiety Subscale Question, (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.94). SEst, which refers to Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale Question (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.85).


Data Analysis Strategy
In the Social Interaction Anxiety Scale responses (SA), items 5, 9, and 11 are reverse keyed. In the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (SEst), items 2, 5, 6, 8, and 9 are reverse keyed. No item in Close Relationship Anxiety Subscale Question (AA) is reverse keyed.

Measures
In this BFI data set, the 5 factors refer to the 5 composites included in the Big Five Inventory. Openness, which indicates one’s open-mindedness, creativity, and likelihood to embrace new experiences (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.6). Conscientiousness, which refers to one’s tendency to be reliable, organized, and disciplined (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.72). Extraversion, which refers to one’s social interactions and emotional expression (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.76). Agreeableness, which refers to one’s tendency to cooperate or desire to compete (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.7). and Neuroticism which refers to one’s tendency toward depression, anxiety, or negative feelings (Cronbach’s alpha =0.81).


Data Analysis Strategy
The data for variables O2, C4, E1, E2, and A1 were reverse keyed.
